TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Crib — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "crib" through a rehearsal: teddy goes to bed first, the same sentence lands at the rail every night, and the bed word becomes the period at the end of the day.

What is this?

The crib is the toddler’s own bed — bars, mattress, the yellow blanket — and the word that ends every day when it is said in the same place at the same time.

What does it mean?

"Crib" is a place word with a promise inside: sleep is next. Toddlers who can name the destination fight the journey less.

What does the child need to know?

You need the crib, one sentence and a teddy with a bed of his own (a shoebox works). The sentence — "into the crib, night-night" — is said at the rail, every night, until the child says it first.

Why this matters

Rituals are how toddlers tell time. The crib sentence is the last line of the day’s script; a known last line is what lets a small body let go.

What it teaches

Routine vocabulary, day-night sequencing, gentle transfer (the teddy tuck), and the self-settling that a predictable bed invites.

Words to learn

cribbedsleepnight-nightcozyteddy

Say this to your child

“"Crib! This is your crib — your very own bed. Cozy crib, soft blanket. Into the crib we go… night-night. Sleep tight. The crib is where sleep lives."”

Step by step

  1. At play, introduce teddy’s bed: "teddy is sleepy — into his crib! Night-night, teddy."
  2. Let the toddler do the tucking — sloppiness is love.
  3. Keep teddy’s routine shorter than theirs: he sleeps NOW so the idea is fresh tonight.
  4. At the real bedtime, the same sentence at the rail: "into the crib, night-night." Same words, same spot.
  5. Night after night, drop your voice a little more each word — the sentence itself becomes the wind-down.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "crib" sits under a blue crib with yellow bedding — the bed itself, made and waiting.

Ask your child

"Where do you sleep?" "Where does teddy sleep?" "What do we say at the crib?" (night-night!)

What your child can say or do

Your child might say "nigh-nigh" at the rail, tuck teddy unprompted, or climb in clutching the blanket — the word and the routine shaking hands.

Out in the real world

Beds are everywhere in books and lives — the baby’s crib, grandpa’s big bed, the dog’s basket. "Where does everyone sleep?" is a whole-car-ride game.

Try it together

Sleepy Zoo: every animal needs tucking into a "crib" (boxes, cushions, pots). The zookeeper tucks each one with the bedtime word. Lights out, zoo closed.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is this?" (crib) "Where do YOU sleep?" "Say it at the rail… what do we say?" Bed, point, night-night — the day can end now.

This lesson pairs with the Crib flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
